{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVaC1p88AAAABbjcJbw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BpEKozhFHW-4", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BpEKo", "number": 34, "title": "Reduce routine PR CI to under 10 minutes while retaining nightly full RTL regressions", "body": "## Problem

WebRTL's normal PR feedback is too slow: the latest successful **Full validation** run [41257353210](https://github.com/takahirox/webrtl/actions/runs/41257353210) took **2 h 32 m 53 s** end to end. Its Firefox static job took about 2 h 31 m and Chromium about 1 h 58 m. The heavy part is the 260-cartridge SNES corpus and reset replays in the real browser/CXXRTL runtime, not Pages publishing, which now completes in roughly one minute.

This is unacceptable for routine development iteration in a **general-purpose RTL compiler/simulator**. #30 already eliminated repeated SNES compilation across batches; the remaining simulated workload cannot realistically be reduced 15-fold simply by further deduplicating compilation.

## Goal

**A developer gets trustworthy pass/fail PR feedback in 10 minutes or less on the standard GitHub Actions Ubuntu runners**, including setup and browser/compiler smoke validation. Preserve all existing regression fixtures and assertions in a separately scheduled/on-demand comprehensive validation workflow.

This explicitly changes the previous policy of running the full 260-cartridge corpus on *every* PR. Do **not** call a reduced PR suite “full” or imply that a quick pass proves exhaustive SNES compatibility. Optimize for fast, honest, high-signal feedback rather than hiding failures.

## Implementation direction

1. **Fast PR gate:** Run for every PR to `main` (and on updates), with a clear named aggregate status. Reuse the existing lightweight Pages build/smoke if possible instead of rebuilding static assets repeatedly. Include Python/Node unit checks; browser-only edited RTL → generated Wasm → executable result; generic project/clock/reset or Fast→Debug→Fast continuity; relevant Canvas and audio boundaries; and at least a focused genuine SNES RTL cartridge/CPU/PPU/APU/control smoke when feasible under the budget. Preserve independent expectations and do not replace circuit tests with hardcoded/mock results. The necessary browser combinations may be chosen deliberately, not multiplied across every fixture.
2. **Run relevant changed-area checks:** For substantial changes to SNES RTL, compiler, runtime, or debugger, use a representative bounded selection covering the affected behavior (CPU, PPU, DMA, APU, cartridge, reset, video/audio, as applicable). Define deterministic selection or simple file-based rules; prevent broad RTL changes from silently getting a trivial-only check. Do not accidentally run 260 cartridges in the fast lane. A small browser smoke that is insufficient to validate a specific change must trigger additional focused/manual review validation, with explicit evidence, rather than falsely promising exhaustive pre-merge coverage.
3. **Retain full coverage:** Run the existing complete Chromium+Firefox 260-cartridge/29-replay suite, trusted-local native checks and all other regressions on a **nightly schedule and `workflow_dispatch`**. Preserve all fixtures, oracles, loops, and immutable-Wasm reuse. Full failures must be visible, linkable, and actionable, not discarded or reclassified as success; document how maintainers investigate them. Keep the full suite runnable locally. Do not make this multi-hour workflow an unconditional required check for every PR, since that defeats the 10-minute goal.
4. **CI semantics:** Keep artifact provenance, same-commit checking, cancellation of superseded PR checks, a non-skippable aggregate fast status, and the separate quick Pages publish workflow. Avoid redundant checkout/npm/browser setup where practical. Do not simply raise timeouts, skip assertions, set `continue-on-error`, or mark cancelled jobs as passed. Make check names and documentation clearly distinguish fast PR confidence from scheduled comprehensive coverage.
5. **Document the deliberate trade-off:** Fast PR CI checks critical paths quickly but cannot guarantee all 260 independent cartridge variants on each change. Describe what is guaranteed before merge, what runs nightly/on-demand, any requirement for additional affected-area validation, and how to respond to a failed full run.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] **An actual successful GitHub Actions Ubuntu PR run for the final revision finishes in under 600 seconds**, measured from run creation through aggregate result (report queue separately). Set job/workflow time budgets to fail clearly on overrun; do not claim success from only a local run or YAML inspection.
- [ ] Fast PR checks genuinely compile modified/user-supplied RTL into Wasm and validate observable circuit behavior; include a representative non-SNES example and a bounded SNES hardware integration smoke when feasible. At least one regression rejects a deliberate RTL, frontend or worker behavior defect.
- [ ] Changed-area selection cannot silently omit all important tests for broad compiler/runtime/SNES modifications; document exactly which behavior is exercised on each PR and when targeted extra validation is required.
- [ ] The existing full regression is still executable on schedule and manually, with unchanged comprehensive fixture set (260 SNES cartridge cases and reset replays, cross-browser pixels/PCM and other device checks, trusted-local integration, Python/Node and prior examples). Explicitly verify test discovery/fixture counts and workflow trigger behavior.
- [ ] The full regression's pass/fail is not misrepresented as a fast PR result. Failures are surfaced and triaged, including after a merge, and fast/full check statuses are distinct.
- [ ] GitHub Pages continues to deploy only from successful static build/smoke on `main` and does not wait for the multi-hour comprehensive suite.
- [ ] Workflow event/concurrency/job-dependency invariants, source/artifact identity, failure propagation and actual time are verified. No manual-only gate, external compiler server, loss of RTL privacy, or SNES-only modification to WebRTL's normal project model.
- [ ] README, developer flow/review guidance and CI performance record reflect the new policy and include commands for focused PR and complete scheduled/manual tests.

## Timing context

- Successful PR full run [41257353210](https://github.com/takahirox/webrtl/actions/runs/41257353210): 152m53s elapsed; static Chromium 118m01s, Firefox 150m54s.
- Successful Pages push deployment [41267991542](https://github.com/takahirox/webrtl/actions/runs/41267991542): 64s.
- [#30 measurements](https://github.com/takahirox/webrtl/blob/main/docs/regression-performance.md) already show the full corpus's runtime and compilation reuse; keep that work.

## Out of scope

- Replacing RTL computation with a JavaScript SNES emulator.
- Claiming all hardware behavior was validated by a small PR smoke.
- Achieving an entire 260-cartridge/full-browser corpus in 10 minutes at the expense of correctness.
- Conflating this **CI latency** initiative with the separate Fast Mode **RTL simulator throughput** problem.

## Related

- #3 — WebRTL project vision
- #22 — integrated SNES RTL
- #26 — Pages publication separated from full checks
- #28 — testing/CI performance principles
- #30 — compilation reuse and current full regression budgets
- #32 — generic Fast/Debug simulation
